cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Asmat bis pole — a carved ancestor pole with superimposed human figures and an openwork projecting "wing" (cemen) — a signature ritual object of the Asmat people of New Guinea.

physical.title: pole; post
physical.summary: Carved wood bis pole with three superimposed human figures, their arms and legs carved free. The eyes are inlaid with black gum or resin and plaited vegetable fibre bands round arms, legs and waists. A projection is springing from a lower figure carved in openwork with human figures, S scrolls and terminating in a bird's head. Below the human figures on the main pole is a cavity with a projection of triangular section. The whole has been coloured white. The base, which had rotted, was replaced with timber of similar appearance.
